source: distilled from reference/components/*/page.mdx + *.tsx (offline mirror of github.com/ibelick/motion-primitives, MIT)
purpose: Structured per-component knowledge for design-system migration workflows: props, shadcn/@kit pairing, migration-use, adapt-notes, reduced-motion guard.

components.name: Accordion
components.intent: Use this when you need a height/opacity-animated collapsible disclosure group with custom expand/collapse motion variants.

props.name: children
props.desc: The content elements of the accordion.

props.name: className
props.desc: Optional CSS class for styling the accordion container.

props.name: transition
props.desc: Transition settings from motion for animation effects.

props.name: variants
props.desc: Custom variants for expanded and collapsed states.

props.name: expandedValue
props.desc: Controlled expanded value.

props.name: onValueChange
props.desc: Callback function when the expanded value changes.

components.shadcn_pairing: Drop-in motion alternative to shadcn's Accordion primitive (which wraps Radix). Same Accordion/AccordionItem/AccordionTrigger/AccordionContent compound shape, so it composes inside any Card or section as a collapsible FAQ/disclosure list. Trigger is a real button so it pairs with Badge/icon children; the group className enables group-data-[expanded] icon rotation like a shadcn ChevronDown.
components.migration_use: Replace hand-rolled Tailwind disclosure markup — a div with a click-toggled useState boolean, a button header, and a content div gated by `hidden`/`max-h-0 overflow-hidden` transition classes — with the Accordion compound. Wire each section's `value` to AccordionItem, move the header into AccordionTrigger, the body into AccordionContent, and delete the manual open-state booleans and max-height CSS hacks; the height:auto/opacity motion variants replace the brittle max-h transition. Use expandedValue/onValueChange only if a parent must control which panel is open.
components.adapt_notes: Upstream imports from 'motion/react' (motion, AnimatePresence, MotionConfig, Transition, Variant, Variants) — if the kit is on framer-motion, rewrite to 'framer-motion' (named exports are identical, no prop renames). Imports cn from '@/lib/utils' — repoint to the kit's cn (e.g. '@kit/ui/utils' or local '~/lib/utils'). File already declares 'use client' at top; keep it — it uses useState/useContext and must be a client component. Single-open semantics by design (toggleItem nulls the prior value); for multi-open you'd fork the provider to a Set. No defaults are emitted by the API table, so callers must supply transition/variants for non-instant motion.
components.reduced_motion: No prefers-reduced-motion guard in source — AnimatePresence + the height/opacity variants always animate. Wrap the subtree in <MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"> (motion respects the OS setting and drops transform/opacity tweens) or read useReducedMotion() and pass a near-zero `transition={{ duration: 0 }}` so the panel snaps open instead of sliding.

components.name: Animated Background
components.intent: Use this when a selected/hovered item in a list, menu, tab strip, or segmented control needs a smooth sliding background to signal the active selection.

props.name: children
props.type: ReactElement with 'data-id' string attribute array or single element
props.desc: The content to be displayed within the animated background. Each child must have a unique data-id attribute to ensure correct functionality.

props.name: defaultValue
props.desc: The default value to be used as the active item identifier.

props.name: onValueChange
props.desc: Callback function that is called when the active item changes.

props.name: className
props.desc: The class name to apply to the animated background for custom styling.

props.name: transition
props.desc: The transition effect from motion for animation effects.

props.name: enableHover
props.desc: Enables or disables the hover effect. When enableHover is true, spacing between children cannot be added.

components.shadcn_pairing: Wraps a Tabs/TabsList trigger row, a list/grid of selectable Card or Button items, or a custom segmented control. It is the shared moving indicator behind whatever child carries the active data-id — think of it as the animated "active pill" layer you drop around shadcn triggers/menu items to give them a single sliding highlight instead of per-item background toggles.
components.migration_use: A migration agent applies this where raw markup renders a row of buttons/links/cards and toggles a static highlight class on the active one (e.g. className={cn('px-3 py-1', active === id && 'bg-muted rounded')} with onClick={() => setActive(id)}). Replace that per-item conditional background with a single <AnimatedBackground defaultValue={active} onValueChange={setActive} className="bg-muted rounded">{items.map(i => <button key={i.id} data-id={i.id}>{i.label}</button>)}</AnimatedBackground> — the highlight becomes one shared layoutId element that slides between selections instead of hard-cutting per item. Set enableHover for nav/menu hover-follow behavior.
components.adapt_notes: Upstream imports motion via `import { AnimatePresence, Transition, motion } from 'motion/react'` — in a framer-motion repo rewrite to `from 'framer-motion'` (same AnimatePresence/motion/Transition API, no prop renames needed). Requires the 'use client' directive (already present) because it uses useState/useEffect/useId — keep it for App Router. Imports cn from `@/lib/utils`; repoint to the kit's cn helper (e.g. `@kit/ui/utils` or local `~/lib/utils`). Contract gotcha: every child MUST carry a unique `data-id` string prop or selection breaks; the component clones children and injects key/className/data-checked plus the click-or-hover handlers, so children must forward those (native elements do, custom components must spread props). When enableHover is true, do not add spacing between children.
components.reduced_motion: Does NOT guard prefers-reduced-motion — the layoutId/opacity slide always animates regardless of OS setting. To respect it, wrap with motion's MotionConfig reducedMotion="user", or pass a transition prop conditioned on a useReducedMotion() check (e.g. transition={prefersReduced ? { duration: 0 } : undefined}) so the background snaps instead of sliding for users who opt out.

components.name: Animated Group
components.intent: Use this when a list/grid of children should reveal with a staggered entrance animation.

props.name: children
props.desc: The child elements to be animated.

props.name: variants
props.desc: Custom variants for container and item animations.

props.name: preset
props.desc: Preset entrance animation applied to each child (docs list a subset; the .tsx PresetType adds zoom/flip/bounce/rotate/swing).

props.name: as
props.desc: The HTML element to render the container as.

props.name: asChild
props.desc: The HTML element each child is wrapped/rendered as.

props.name: className
props.desc: Optional CSS class for styling the container.

components.shadcn_pairing: Wraps any list/grid container of Cards, Badges, or list items. Drop it around a mapped collection (feature Cards, pricing tiles, a grid of avatars, dashboard stat tiles, command-menu results) so the whole group staggers in. It is a structural container, not a leaf primitive — it composes ABOVE shadcn components rather than replacing one. Pairs naturally with the children of a section, CardContent grid, or Tabs panel reveal.
components.migration_use:
Replace a raw mapped container like `
{items.map(i => )}
` with `{items.map(...)}`. The engineer lifts the grid/flex className onto AnimatedGroup, keeps the same children, and gets staggered entrance for free. Also upgrades static feature lists, testimonial walls, and stat-tile rows that currently render with no motion. Note: each child is wrapped in an extra motion element, so move per-item layout classes (e.g. flex/col-span) onto the child itself, not relying on the wrapper being the direct grid item — or pass `asChild`/`as` to control the wrapper tag.
components.adapt_notes: Upstream imports `motion` and `Variants` from `motion/react` (the modern Motion package) — in a framer-motion repo rewrite the import to `framer-motion`; the `Variants` type and the `motion.create()` API are equivalent in recent framer-motion, but older framer-motion versions expose `motion(Component)` instead of `motion.create()` — swap if the build complains. File already declares `'use client'` (required — it uses motion + React.useMemo/Children), keep it for Next.js App Router. No `cn`/clsx helper used — `className` is passed through raw, so add `cn()` only if you want to merge. Docs vs source mismatch: the docs API table lists presets `fade | slide | scale | blur-sm | blur-slide` (note `blur-sm`), but the actual .tsx PresetType key is `blur` and adds `zoom | flip | bounce | rotate | swing` — trust the .tsx. No external shared deps; self-contained.
components.reduced_motion: No prefers-reduced-motion guard. The component hardcodes initial='hidden' / animate='visible' and spring transitions with zero accessibility opt-out — motion-sensitive users get the full stagger/blur/bounce. To respect it, wrap with Motion's `useReducedMotion()` hook and, when true, pass `preset={undefined}` plus an instant container variant (staggerChildren: 0, items hidden→visible with no offset/filter), or render children plainly. Alternatively gate via CSS `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`. Spring presets (zoom/flip/bounce/rotate/swing) are the most jarring and should collapse to a plain fade or no animation under reduced motion.

components.name: Animated Number
components.intent: Use this when a numeric value should spring-count to its target instead of snapping.

props.name: value
props.desc: The number to be animated.

props.name: className
props.desc: Optional CSS class for styling the number item container.

props.name: springOptions
props.desc: Spring options from motion for the animation.

props.name: as
props.desc: The HTML tag to render the number in.

components.shadcn_pairing: Enhances the numeric value inside any shadcn Card/stat tile — wrap the displayed count in a CardContent, Badge, or KPI/metric block. Composes WITH Card (dashboard metric tiles), Badge (animated count badges), and any value/number slot in a list/grid of stats.
components.migration_use:
A migration agent replaces a static numeric span in a metric/KPI tile — e.g. raw `{revenue}` or `
{count}
` — with ``. The component already injects `tabular-nums`, so drop that utility from the original markup. Upgrades any place where a live/fetched number is painted directly, giving count-up motion on mount and on every value change (it re-springs via useEffect on value).
components.adapt_notes: Upstream imports from `motion/react` (the current Motion package) — if the kit standardizes on legacy `framer-motion`, rewrite the import to `framer-motion` and note `motion.create(...)` is `motion(...)` in older framer-motion versions (rename needed there). Requires `'use client'` (uses useSpring/useTransform/useEffect hooks) — keep the directive when dropping into a Next.js App Router server-component tree. Imports `cn` from `@/lib/utils`; in @kit/ui repos repoint to the kit's `cn` helper (e.g. `@kit/ui/utils` or local `~/lib/utils`). No prop renames vs framer-motion API surface; SpringOptions is the same shape. Note the runtime formats with `Math.round(...).toLocaleString()` — integers only, locale-grouped thousands; for decimals/currency you must fork the transform.
components.reduced_motion: Does NOT guard prefers-reduced-motion — the spring runs unconditionally on mount and on every value change. To respect it, wrap with a `useReducedMotion()` check (from motion/react) and either pass a near-instant `springOptions` (e.g. high stiffness / zero-ish duration) or short-circuit to render the plain `value.toLocaleString()` when reduced motion is requested.

components.name: Border Trail
components.intent: Use this when you want a glowing light trail that endlessly travels around a container's border to signal "live", "loading", or "active focus".

props.name: className
props.desc: Additional CSS classes for styling the border trail (e.g. recolor the default bg-zinc-500 dot to a brand gradient).

props.name: size
props.desc: Size of the animated border effect — width of the traveling square dot and the corner radius of its offset path.

props.name: transition
props.desc: Custom transition settings for the animation; overrides the default { repeat: Infinity, duration: 5, ease: 'linear' }.

props.name: onAnimationComplete
props.desc: Callback function triggered when the animation completes.

props.name: style
props.desc: (impl-only, not in docs API table) Extra inline styles merged onto the moving dot, after width/offsetPath are applied.

components.shadcn_pairing: Drops INSIDE any relatively-positioned shadcn Card, Input, Textarea, or section as an absolutely-positioned overlay child. It enhances a container rather than replacing one — wrap a Card to mark it as "processing/streaming", or sit inside an Input/Textarea to draw focus to an active field. Composes with Badge-style "Live" affordances on a tile.
components.migration_use: Replace a hand-rolled animated-border hack — a wrapper div with `animate-pulse ring-2 ring-primary` or a `before:`/`after:` conic-gradient `@keyframes spin` border trick — on a Card/Input/section. Make the parent `relative` (and `rounded-*` since the trail inherits `rounded-[inherit]`), then drop `<BorderTrail />` as the last child. For a loading state, gate render on `isLoading` and recolor via `className`.
components.adapt_notes: Upstream imports `motion`/`Transition` from `motion/react` — if the kit is on legacy framer-motion, rewrite to `framer-motion` (same `motion.div`, `Transition`, `animate`, `transition`, `onAnimationComplete` API; no prop renames). `'use client'` IS required (uses motion animation) — keep it; in a Server Component, wrap or import into a client boundary. `cn` is imported from `@/lib/utils` — repoint to the kit's helper (`@kit/ui` re-exports `cn`). No shared hooks. Relies on modern CSS `offset-path`/`mask-composite`; verify browser-target support. Parent MUST be `position: relative` and rounded or the trail mis-clips.
components.reduced_motion: No guard — the default transition is `repeat: Infinity` and runs unconditionally, ignoring `prefers-reduced-motion`. Add a guard before adopting: read `useReducedMotion()` from motion/react and either skip rendering `<BorderTrail />` or pass a `transition` with `repeat: 0`/`duration: 0` (or a static frame) when it returns true, since a perpetual loop is exactly the kind of motion that policy targets.

components.name: Carousel
components.intent: use this when you need a drag/swipe-able, spring-animated slide track with optional arrow nav and dot indicators, controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: children
props.desc: The content elements of the carousel.

props.name: className
props.desc: Optional CSS class for styling the carousel container.

props.name: initialIndex
props.desc: Initial index of the active carousel item.

props.name: index
props.desc: Controlled index of the active carousel item.

props.name: onIndexChange
props.desc: Callback function when the active index changes.

props.name: disableDrag
props.desc: Whether dragging is disabled.

components.shadcn_pairing: A self-contained alternative to the shadcn `Carousel` (embla) primitive — same compound shape (Carousel / CarouselContent / CarouselItem / CarouselNavigation / CarouselIndicator) but motion-driven instead of embla. Wraps any list/grid of Cards, image tiles, or testimonial/feature sections; CarouselNavigation behaves like a Button pair and CarouselIndicator like a Tabs/dot value selector. Use it to give a horizontal Card row swipe + spring transitions; pairs naturally with Card-based content and a Tabs-style controlled `index`.
components.migration_use: Replace a hand-rolled Tailwind horizontal scroller — a `<div class="flex overflow-x-auto snap-x">` with manually mapped slide divs and DIY prev/next `<button>`s — with this compound API: wrap the track in `<Carousel><CarouselContent>`, convert each slide to `<CarouselItem className="basis-1/3">` (use `basis-*` for multi-up, `-ml-4`/`pl-4` for gutters), and drop in `<CarouselNavigation/>` + `<CarouselIndicator/>` instead of bespoke arrow/dot markup. Swap `snap-x` scroll for the controlled `index`/`onIndexChange` pair to drive external state. Adds drag-to-swipe and spring physics the raw scroller lacks.
components.adapt_notes: Upstream imports from `motion/react` (`motion`, `Transition`, `useMotionValue`) — keep as-is if the kit ships `motion`, otherwise rewrite to `framer-motion` (same named exports, no prop renames). Needs `'use client'` (already at top) — it uses useState/useEffect/useRef, IntersectionObserver, and drag handlers, so it cannot be a server component. Imports `cn` from `@/lib/utils` — repoint to the kit's `cn` (`@kit/ui` / `~/lib/utils`). Icons come from `lucide-react` (ChevronLeft/ChevronRight) which the kit already has. Exports a `useCarousel()` hook (throws outside provider) for building custom indicators. No framer-vs-motion prop drift.
components.reduced_motion: No guard — the spring `translateX` animation and drag transition always run; the source never reads `useReducedMotion()` or `prefers-reduced-motion`. To respect it, wrap with `useReducedMotion()` from motion/react and pass a near-instant `transition` (e.g. `{ duration: 0 }`) to CarouselContent plus `disableDrag` when reduced motion is preferred, or gate the whole component behind a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` fallback that renders a plain scrollable list.

components.name: Cursor
components.intent: Use this when you want a custom spring-animated cursor replacing the native pointer, globally or scoped to one hover region.

props.name: children
props.desc: Children to be rendered within the custom cursor. Mandatory.

props.name: className
props.desc: Optional CSS class for styling the custom cursor container.

props.name: springConfig
props.desc: Configuration for the spring physics used in the cursor's movement.

props.name: attachToParent
props.desc: If true, the cursor will only be visible when hovering over its parent component.

props.name: variants
props.desc: Variants for controlling the animation states with specific properties for initial, animate, and exit states.

props.name: onPositionChange
props.desc: Callback function that is called when the cursor position changes.

components.shadcn_pairing: Not a shadcn primitive wrapper — it is a page/section-level overlay that ENHANCES any interactive region. Scope it (attachToParent) over a Card, hero section, Button, or pricing grid to swap the OS pointer for branded cursor art; pair with Tooltip/HoverCard-style affordances on the same region. Global mode dresses the whole app shell.
components.migration_use: Replaces ad-hoc `cursor-pointer`/custom-cursor CSS (e.g. `style={{ cursor: 'url(...)' }}` or a hand-rolled mousemove listener positioning an absolutely-placed div). An engineer drops `<Cursor attachToParent>...<img/></Cursor>` inside the relative-positioned section that previously had bespoke cursor CSS, and removes the manual mousemove/transform plumbing. For a site-wide custom cursor, mount one `<Cursor>` near the root instead of global `* { cursor: ... }` rules.
components.adapt_notes: Upstream import is `motion/react` (Motion v11+, the renamed framer-motion); on a kit still on framer-motion, rewrite to `import { motion, useMotionValue, useSpring, AnimatePresence, type SpringOptions, type Transition, type Variant } from 'framer-motion'`. REQUIRES `'use client'` — uses useEffect/useRef/useState, window, document.body.style, and DOM listeners. Imports `cn` from `@/lib/utils`; in @kit point to `@kit/ui/utils` (or `~/lib/utils`). PROP-SHAPE MISMATCH to fix: the docs table types `onPositionChange` as `(position: {x,y}) => void`, but the actual .tsx calls `onPositionChange?.(e.clientX, e.clientY)` with the type `(x: number, y: number) => void` — trust the implementation (two positional args), not the table. Side effects to know: in global mode it sets `document.body.style.cursor = 'none'`, so SSR-safe only because guarded behind useEffect. Note the parent mouseenter/mouseleave listeners are added and removed with different function identities (cleanup does not actually detach them) — a known leak to patch if you scope many instances.
components.reduced_motion: No prefers-reduced-motion guard in source — it always spring-tracks the pointer and hides the native cursor. Add a `useReducedMotion()` (from motion/react) check: when true, pass `springConfig={{ duration: 0 }}` (or skip the spring and bind cursorX/Y directly) so the custom cursor snaps instead of lagging, and consider restoring `document.body.style.cursor = 'auto'` entirely so motion-sensitive users keep the native pointer. Wrap the visibility/exit transition in the same guard to disable the AnimatePresence fade.

components.name: Dialog
components.intent: use this when you need a modal overlay whose open/close is spring/variant-animated, not the instant-toggle shadcn Dialog

props.name: children
props.desc: Children to be rendered within the dialog.

props.name: variants
props.desc: Variants for controlling the animation states with specific properties for initial, animate, and exit states.

props.name: transition
props.desc: Transition settings from framer-motion for animation effects.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.desc: If true, the dialog will be open by default.

props.name: open
props.desc: Controlled open state of the dialog.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.desc: Callback function that is called when the dialog's open state changes.

components.shadcn_pairing: Drop-in replacement for shadcn/ui Dialog (Radix). Exposes the same compound surface — Dialog / DialogTrigger / DialogContent / DialogHeader / DialogTitle / DialogDescription / DialogClose — so any Radix-based modal maps 1:1, but swaps Radix's CSS-only data-state transitions for Framer Motion variants/transition. Pairs with Button as the trigger child and wraps any Card/form/section as content.
components.migration_use: Replace a hand-rolled Tailwind modal — a fixed inset-0 backdrop div plus a centered absolute panel toggled by a useState boolean and conditional `hidden`/opacity classes — with this compound API. Lift the trigger element into DialogTrigger, the panel body into DialogContent (it already does the portal, native <dialog> showModal, top-1/2 left-1/2 centering, backdrop:bg-black/50 backdrop-blur, scroll-lock, ESC-cancel, and click-outside-to-close), and the X button into DialogClose. Wire existing open state through `open`/`onOpenChange` for controlled use, or delete it entirely and rely on the built-in uncontrolled state + `defaultOpen`. Net effect: focus-trapped, scroll-locked, animated entry/exit for free instead of an un-animated div toggle.
components.adapt_notes: Import is `motion/react` (Motion v11+), not `framer-motion` — if the kit pins framer-motion, rewrite the import line to `from 'framer-motion'` (Variants/Transition/AnimatePresence/motion all re-export identically; `motion.dialog` exists in both). Already declares 'use client' at top — keep it; it uses useState/useRef/useEffect/useContext/createPortal so it cannot be a server component. Uses the standard `cn` helper from `@/lib/utils` — repoint to the kit's `@kit/ui` cn if paths differ. Depends on a local `usePreventScroll` hook at `@/hooks/usePreventScroll` (iOS scroll-lock) and `X` from lucide-react — both must be vendored or the import paths fixed. No prop renames vs framer-motion; prop surface is the component's own (variants/transition/open/onOpenChange/defaultOpen). Note it portals into document.body via DialogContent's `container` prop (default document.body) and renders a real native <dialog> element, so global `dialog`/`backdrop:` CSS resets can interfere.
components.reduced_motion: No guard. The component hardcodes scale/opacity variants and a 0.2s easeOut transition and never consults `prefers-reduced-motion`, so motion-sensitive users still get the scale-in/out. To respect it, read `useReducedMotion()` from motion/react in a wrapper and pass a reduced `variants` prop (e.g. opacity-only `{initial:{opacity:0},animate:{opacity:1}}` with `transition={{duration:0}}` or a near-instant fade) when it returns true, or gate the scale via a CSS `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` override on the dialog element.

components.name: Disclosure
components.intent: Use this when you want a collapsible/expandable content panel with animated height + opacity transitions.

props.name: open
props.desc: Controls the visibility of the content.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.desc: Callback function to handle changes in the open state.

props.name: children
props.desc: The content to be toggled, typically includes DisclosureTrigger and DisclosureContent.

props.name: className
props.desc: Additional CSS classes for the container.

props.name: variants
props.desc: Custom animation variants for expanded and collapsed states.

props.name: transition
props.desc: Custom transition settings for the motion animations.

components.shadcn_pairing: A motion-native alternative to/enhancer for shadcn Accordion and Collapsible. Composes the same trigger + content pair (Disclosure / DisclosureTrigger / DisclosureContent mirrors Collapsible / CollapsibleTrigger / CollapsibleContent) but adds animated height+opacity. Wrap inside any Card to make an expandable section, FAQ row, or "show more" detail panel; the trigger child can be a shadcn Button or any clickable element.
components.migration_use: Replace hand-rolled Tailwind collapse markup — a useState boolean toggling `hidden`/`max-h-0 overflow-hidden` on a content div with no animation, or a `<details>`/`<summary>` block — with `<Disclosure open={x} onOpenChange={setX}><DisclosureTrigger><button>…</button></DisclosureTrigger><DisclosureContent>…</DisclosureContent></Disclosure>`. The trigger child automatically gets role=button, aria-expanded, tabIndex, and Enter/Space keyboard handling cloned onto it, so it upgrades both the animation and the a11y of raw toggle markup. Ideal for FAQ items, accordion rows, "read more" panels, and expandable card sections.
components.adapt_notes: Upstream import is `motion/react` (AnimatePresence, motion, MotionConfig, Transition, Variant, Variants) — keep as-is if the kit has `motion` installed; rewrite to `framer-motion` only if that is the installed package (API is identical, just the package name differs). Imports `cn` from `@/lib/utils` — repoint to the kit's cn helper (e.g. `@kit/ui/utils` or local `~/lib/utils`). File already declares `'use client'` (line 1) and is required since it uses useState/useId/useEffect/createContext — must stay a client component. Note: Disclosure only renders `React.Children.toArray(children)[0]` and `[1]`, so it expects EXACTLY two children (trigger then content) in that order. Props match framer-motion conventions; no renames needed.
components.reduced_motion: Does NOT guard prefers-reduced-motion — it animates height 0↔auto and opacity 0↔1 unconditionally via fixed BASE_VARIANTS in DisclosureContent, with no useReducedMotion check. To respect it, either wrap in a `<MotionConfig reducedMotion="user">` ancestor (cheapest, since the component already uses MotionConfig internally for `transition`), or read `useReducedMotion()` from motion/react and pass a near-instant `transition={{ duration: 0 }}` (or collapse variants) when true so content snaps open/closed instead of sliding.

components.name: Dock
components.intent: Use this when you want a macOS-style magnifying icon toolbar where items scale up as the cursor passes over them.

props.name: children
props.desc: The child elements to be animated (DockItem nodes).

props.name: className
props.desc: Optional CSS class for styling the component.

props.name: spring
props.desc: Spring options from motion for animation effects.

props.name: magnification
props.desc: The scaling factor applied to a dock item on hover.

props.name: distance
props.desc: The distance from the center of a dock item at which the magnification animation starts.

props.name: panelHeight
props.desc: The resting height of the dock panel (px) before hover expansion.

components.shadcn_pairing: Composes a horizontal toolbar/navigation strip — think a shadcn Menubar or a row of icon Buttons inside a fixed bottom bar. Each DockItem wraps a Button-sized icon target (role="button"), and DockLabel is effectively a Tooltip surface (role="tooltip") that auto-shows on hover/focus. Use it to upgrade any persistent app launcher, command bar, or icon nav into a magnifying dock.
components.migration_use: Replace a static row of icon buttons — e.g. a `<div className="flex gap-4">` containing several `<button><Icon/></button>` (a bottom nav bar, floating action cluster, or app launcher) — with `<Dock>` wrapping `<DockItem onClick={...}><DockIcon><Icon/></DockIcon><DockLabel>name</DockLabel></DockItem>` per entry. The raw flex row's hover:scale Tailwind utilities and title-attribute tooltips get superseded by cursor-distance magnification plus the animated DockLabel tooltip.
components.adapt_notes: Upstream imports from `motion/react` (Motion, the framer-motion successor); if the kit is still on `framer-motion`, change the import to `framer-motion` — the named exports (motion, MotionValue, useMotionValue, useSpring, useTransform, AnimatePresence, type SpringOptions) and APIs are identical. File is a client component: keep the `'use client'` directive (uses refs, context, useState, useEffect, mouse handlers). Uses the `cn` helper from `@/lib/utils` — repoint to the kit's `cn` (e.g. `@kit/ui/utils` or local `~/lib/utils`). No prop renames vs framer-motion. Note: DockItem passes `width`/`isHovered` to children via `Children.map`+`cloneElement`, so custom children placed directly under DockItem should tolerate extra injected props; prefer the provided DockIcon/DockLabel.
components.reduced_motion: No guard — it does not check prefers-reduced-motion; magnification and the height spring always animate from raw mouseX/useSpring. Lift the branches into an ordered `children` array, hoist the discriminant to a numeric `activeIndex` (map tab key/step name → index), and wrap in `<TransitionPanel activeIndex={i} variants={...} transition={...}>` so state changes cross-fade/slide via AnimatePresence popLayout instead of jumping. Common upgrade targets: tab bodies, onboarding step cards, settings sub-panels, and image/quote rotators.
components.adapt_notes: Source imports from `motion/react` (modern Motion package: AnimatePresence, Transition, Variant, motion, MotionProps) — keep as-is on Motion v11+; if the kit still pins `framer-motion`, swap the import to `framer-motion` (same symbol names, no prop renames). Requires the `'use client'` directive (already present) since it uses AnimatePresence/motion hooks — keep it when porting into an RSC tree. Uses the `cn` helper from `@/lib/utils`; in @kit/ui repos retarget to the kit's `cn` (e.g. `@kit/ui/utils` or local `~/lib/utils`). One gotcha: `children` must be an array indexed by `activeIndex` (not a single node), and each child needs a stable identity — the component keys the motion.div by `activeIndex`, so out-of-range or non-array children render nothing.
components.reduced_motion: Does NOT guard prefers-reduced-motion — animations always play via the supplied variants/transition regardless of OS setting. To make it accessible, either gate the motion with Motion's `useReducedMotion()` hook (pass a no-op/instant transition or center-only variants when it returns true), wrap the app in a `MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"`, or add a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` fallback. Without one of these the index swap animates for users who requested reduced motion.
